back: Put each variant of an algorithm behind one interface so the user of it can swap variants at runtime.
Context (uses the strategy), Strategy (the shared interface), Concrete strategies (the variants).

front: Which principle does Strategy apply most directly?
back: Encapsulate what varies, and favour composition over inheritance.
The client or a configuration, from outside the context. The context only calls it.

front: Strategy vs State in one line?
back: Strategy: the client picks the behaviour. State: the object switches its own behaviour as it changes.

front: Strategy vs Template Method in one line?
back: Strategy swaps the whole algorithm by composition. Template Method varies steps by inheritance.
Pass a function. A one-method, stateless strategy does not need a class.

front: How to pick a strategy without if/elif?
back: Look it up in a dictionary keyed by name, or use a small factory.
More small types and one extra level of indirection; clients must know which strategy to choose.
